item.title: Iranians debate whether the war is worth it
item.summary: As the war in Iran enters its second month, and President Trump signals an end to the war, many Iranians are urging the U.S and Israel to keep striking their country.

item.title: A foreign policy adviser to Netanyahu talks about Israel's stance on war with Iran
item.summary: NPR's Juana Summers speaks with Ophir Falk, foreign policy adviser to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, about his country's stance on war with Iran and Hezbollah.

item.title: Judge rules White House ballroom construction must halt until Congress OK's it
item.summary: Trump responded to the ruling by complaining that the National Trust for Historic Preservation doesn't appreciate his efforts at "sprucing up" Washington's buildings.

item.title: Suspension lifted for helicopter pilots who hovered near Kid Rock's home
item.summary: The Army pilots who hovered two helicopters near Kid Rock's Tennessee home during a training run while he clapped and saluted have had their suspension lifted, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Tuesday.

item.title: Trump plans to attend Wednesday's Supreme Court hearing on birthright citizenship
item.summary: President Donald Trump plans to sit in on Wednesday's Supreme Court hearing on birthright citizenship, making him the first sitting president to attend oral arguments at the nation's highest court.

item.title: Food assistance slashed for hundreds of thousands of Rohingya refugees trapped in Bangladesh camps
item.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya refugees struggling to survive in Bangladesh's overcrowded camps will see their food assistance slashed starting on Wednesday, raising alarm throughout the increasingly desperate community.

item.title: Tiger Woods says he'll seek treatment after pleading not guilty to DUI
item.summary: Woods said Tuesday he is stepping away to seek treatment, four days after his vehicle crashed in Florida and he was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence. He will miss the Masters for the second straight year.

item.title: Trump signs a new executive order on voting. Experts say he lacks the authority
item.summary: Trump's executive order seeks to create lists of U.S. citizens who are eligible to vote in each state, and instruct the U.S. Postal Service to send mail ballots only to verified voters.

item.title: Runners misled at a qualifier race will still get invites to the world championship
item.summary: The U.S. will nearly double its contingent for the women's half marathon championship to fix what officials call an unprecedented problem: an official vehicle took the leading runners off the course.

item.title: Federal judge finds Trump violated free speech by ordering NPR defunded
item.summary: A U.S. District Court judge found that President Trump's executive order calling for the defunding of NPR and PBS violated the First Amendment.
